biography_notes: Expert PHP and PERL programmer with deep roots in the early web (active 1999-2014).
Experenced a significant life event in March 2014 resulting in the death of his wife; subsequently left the technology industry and remained completely offline for 11 years.
Returned to the digital world in July 2025, finding a vastly changed landscape.
Currently leads Lupopedia with a focus on core engineering principles that favor application-level logic over database-heavy features.

database_philosophy: No Foreign Keys (FK): Database should be dumb storage; logic resides in PHP.
No Triggers/Stored Procedures: All business logic must be in application code.
No Database Functions/Procedures: Keep logic portable and transparent.
No Unsigned Columns: Ensure compatibility with PostgreSQL and other systems.
No Partial Indexes: Avoid 'WHERE' clauses in indexes for maximum cross-DB compatibility.
Precise Queries: Inserts and updates must specify all columns explicitly (no arbitrary column inserts).
data_standards: UTC Always: All timestamps must be in UTC format.
BigInt Timestamps: Store timestamps as BIGINT for precision and portability.
Manual Sync: Rely on exact PHP-driven updates, never database-level automation.
code_standards: PHP 5.3 & 8+ Compatibility: Code must run seamlessly across version 5.3 through 8.x.
No Syntactic Sugar: Avoid short-array tags '[]' in favor of traditional 'array()'.
No Deprecated Functions: Use only stable, long-term supported PHP APIs.
OOP Foundation: Software should be primarily Object-Oriented for maintainability.
